data.title: What Is Booking Holdings (BKNG) Really Building With Its New AI Travel Push?
data.description:

  • The new division is designed to deliver tailored travel solutions for airline, financial services, and loyalty program partners worldwide.
  • Booking Holdings introduced Vayo, which can assemble and book full itineraries across Booking.com and competing travel platforms using AI tools.
  • KAYAK released 28 AI-driven features that support trip planning, search refinement, and booking assistance across its travel metasearch platform.

Booking Holdings operates a global network of travel and restaurant reservation platforms across regions including the US, the Netherlands, and the UK. Expanding its B2B partnerships and AI tools leverages both its consumer reach and its existing relationships with airlines, hotels, and financial services groups.

How does the Booking Partner Division change Booking Holdings' business model exposure?

Folding Booking.com Strategic Partnerships and Rocket Travel into a single Booking Partner Division concentrates a lot more of Booking Holdings' reach into B2B channels. Banks, airlines and other platforms can plug into white label, API and branded solutions that sit on top of the same 4.7 million properties, 500 airlines and 200 car rental providers already in the system.

The new unit and the AI tools around Vayo and KAYAK line up closely with the existing Narrative. That Narrative leans on the Connected Trip ecosystem, AI driven cost savings and a large direct and loyal customer base. They directly relate to the themes around multi product trips, engineering productivity and supplier partnerships that analysts are already using in their scenarios.

The first potential indicator will be how quickly the Booking Partner Division ramps once it is operational in January 2027, especially new contracts with airlines, banks and travel platforms. data.title: Earnings Release: Here's Why Analysts Cut Their Super League Enterprise, Inc. (NASDAQ:SLE) Price Target To US$10.67
data.description:
Shareholders might have noticed that Super League Enterprise, Inc. (NASDAQ:SLE) filed its quarterly result this time last week. The early response was not positive, with shares down 9.8% to US$3.58 in the past week. Revenues of US$2.6m missed forecasts by 15%, but at least statutory losses were much smaller than expected, with per-share losses of US$0.83 coming in 48% smaller than what the analysts had forecast. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. Readers will be glad to know we've aggregated the latest statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their mind on Super League Enterprise after the latest results.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Super League Enterprise's three analysts is for revenues of US$18.5m in 2027. This reflects a huge 57% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. The loss per share is expected to greatly reduce in the near future, narrowing 62% to US$3.91. Before this latest report, the consensus had been expecting revenues of US$18.7m and US$4.52 per share in losses. While the revenue estimates were largely unchanged, sentiment seems to have improved, with the analysts upgrading their numbers and making a cut to losses per share in particular.

See our latest analysis for Super League Enterprise

The consensus price target fell 8.6% to US$10.67despite the forecast for smaller losses next year. It looks like the ongoing lack of profitability is starting to weigh on valuations. Fixating on a single price target can be unwise though, since the consensus target is effectively the average of analyst price targets. As a result, some investors like to look at the range of estimates to see if there are any diverging opinions on the company's valuation. The most optimistic Super League Enterprise analyst has a price target of US$14.00 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at US$6.00. Note the wide gap in analyst price targets? This implies to us that there is a fairly broad range of possible scenarios for the underlying business.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. One thing stands out from these estimates, which is that Super League Enterprise is forecast to grow faster in the future than it has in the past, with revenues expected to display 43% annualised growth until the end of 2027. If achieved, this would be a much better result than the 3.7% annual decline over the past five years. Compare this against analyst estimates for the broader industry, which suggest that (in aggregate) industry revenues are expected to grow 18% annually. So it looks like Super League Enterprise is expected to grow faster than its competitors, at least for a while.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that the analysts made no changes to their forecasts for a loss next year. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of Super League Enterprise's future valuation.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. At Simply Wall St, we have a full range of analyst estimates for Super League Enterprise going out to 2027, and you can see them free on our platform here..

We don't want to rain on the parade too much, but we did also find 4 warning signs for Super League Enterprise (2 can't be ignored!) that you need to be mindful of.

data.title: What Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Doubters Got Wrong
data.description:
Regeneron Pharmaceuticals spent this past year stacking fresh deals and clinical milestones, from the Telix radiopharmaceutical tie‑up to FDA approval of Livsayis for generalized myasthenia gravis. Investors who held Regeneron Pharmaceuticals over the past year are up 25.9%, including dividends. If you were deciding whether to buy on 19 November 2025, you would have seen that bullish and bearish analysts were 31% apart on fair value. Which story about Regeneron’s future did that spread really require you to accept?

This theme extends beyond Regeneron Pharmaceuticals. See which of 36 healthcare AI stocks may still merit a closer look.

The Two Stories Regeneron Investors Were Choosing Between

The shares cost US$703 at the start of the period, so anyone looking at Regeneron Pharmaceuticals then had to decide which of two very different stories to lean toward.

On the upbeat side, the bullish camp saw a Fair Value of US$921, a price implied by assumptions that Dupixent and EYLEA HD could capture far greater US and global market share. That view rested on expectations of 7.9% annual revenue growth and rising profit margins, helped by manufacturing expansion and a broader oncology and hematology portfolio.

The bearish narrative pointed to a Fair Value of US$540, a level based on the idea that biosimilars and US healthcare reforms would steadily erode pricing power. That scenario assumed revenue growth of only 1.4% a year and profit margins falling to 22.5%, with EYLEA and Dupixent exposure, rising R&D costs, and demographic shifts all pressuring future earnings.

What The Evidence Around Regeneron Actually Tested

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals secured FDA approval for Livsayis in generalized myasthenia gravis and reported Q3 2026 revenue of US$5,115.8m and net income of US$1,948.7m, both above Q3 2025 levels, which leaned toward the bullish growth story. Net margin slipped from 38.9% to 38.1%, and the failed melanoma trial with resulting class actions pushed back against the idea of steadily rising profitability. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The key assumption investors were really testing was whether product and partnership wins outpace pricing and pipeline setbacks. For another healthcare stock, you would track whether new approvals, trial readouts, and deal flow show up in higher sales and stable or improving net margin, rather than just in headlines.

What Regeneron’s Current Price Already Assumes

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals now trades at US$923 after a 25.9% gain over the past year. The bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St places its Fair Value below that level, even while accepting strong recent execution across Dupixent, EYLEA HD and newer programs.

That Narrative hinges on whether fresh franchises and pipeline assets genuinely offset pricing, trial and legal pressures. A buyer at today’s price effectively assumes the current breadth of commercial performance and late stage drugs holds up. The question is how those risks affect that belief in durability.

"The main factor that has to go right is that Regeneron Pharmaceuticals converts its broad pipeline and newer franchises such as EYLEA HD, Libtayo, cemdisiran and Pasatru into durable earnings streams that offset pricing pressure and legal and regulatory risks."

One Narrative has put a figure on that disagreement. → See the Narrative with its lower Fair Value, assumptions and all

Another Healthcare Story Nearby

Regeneron keeps the focus on drug pipelines and trial readouts. Your next question is where similar pressures are playing out differently.

One large peer is also leaning harder into oncology, immunology and neuroscience. Management there is trying to tilt toward higher margin specialty treatments.

That same group is reshaping its medical device arm and carving out slower pieces. It is spending heavily on early stage deals that currently weigh on reported earnings.

The bet is that these therapies and platforms eventually justify that upfront hit. If the mix shift works, this could be a very different healthcare story to examine.

data.title: Don't Ignore The Insider Selling In Moog
data.description:
Some Moog Inc. (NYSE:MOG.A) shareholders may be a little concerned to see that the Non-Executive Chairman, John Scannell, recently sold a substantial US$1.0m worth of stock at a price of US$346 per share. However, it's crucial to note that they remain very much invested in the stock and that sale only reduced their holding by 5.3%.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Moog

Notably, that recent sale by Non-Executive Chairman John Scannell was not the only time they sold Moog shares this year. They previously made an even bigger sale of -US$2.1m worth of shares at a price of US$232 per share. That means that even when the share price was below the current price of US$328, an insider wanted to cash in some shares. We generally consider it a negative if insiders have been selling, especially if they did so below the current price, because it implies that they considered a lower price to be reasonable. Please do note, however, that sellers may have a variety of reasons for selling, so we don't know for sure what they think of the stock price. It is worth noting that this sale was only 13% of John Scannell's holding.

John Scannell ditched 15.00k shares over the year. The average price per share was US$283. data.title: There May Be Reason For Hope In Flowers Foods' (NYSE:FLO) Disappointing Earnings
data.description:
Flowers Foods, Inc.'s (NYSE:FLO) earnings announcement last week didn't impress shareholders. While the headline numbers were soft, we believe that investors might be missing some encouraging factors.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

A Closer Look At Flowers Foods' Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Flowers Foods has an accrual ratio of -0.11 for the year to October 2026. Therefore, its statutory earnings were quite a lot less than its free cashflow. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of US$354m, well over the US$30.0m it reported in profit. Flowers Foods shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months. However, that's not all there is to consider. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

Check out our latest analysis for Flowers Foods

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

The Impact Of Unusual Items On Profit

Flowers Foods' profit was reduced by unusual items worth US$190m in the last twelve months, and this helped it produce high cash conversion, as reflected by its unusual items. This is what you'd expect to see where a company has a non-cash charge reducing paper profits. While deductions due to unusual items are disappointing in the first instance, there is a silver lining. We looked at thousands of listed companies and found that unusual items are very often one-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. Flowers Foods took a rather significant hit from unusual items in the year to October 2026. As a result, we can surmise that the unusual items made its statutory profit significantly weaker than it would otherwise be.

Our Take On Flowers Foods' Profit Performance

Considering both Flowers Foods' accrual ratio and its unusual items, we think its statutory earnings are unlikely to exaggerate the company's underlying earnings power. After considering all this, we reckon Flowers Foods' statutory profit probably understates its earnings potential!   • As a triple net lease REIT that collects long term rental income, Realty Income’s valuation largely hinges on how reliably those rents translate into recurring cash that can fund acquisitions and distributions.

On this model, the trust produced roughly $3.89b of adjusted free cash flow over the last twelve months, which is a sizable base for a rental portfolio built on long leases.
